title: LDR Light Sensor Calibration
objective: Verify a photoresistor (LDR) voltage-divider circuit is wired correctly and reads a plausible analog value from ambient light.
safety_notes: Do not short Arduino 5V directly to GND.

steps.title: Place LDR and resistor on breadboard
steps.instruction: Insert the LDR and a 10k resistor into the breadboard forming a voltage divider.

steps.title: Connect LDR output to analog pin
steps.instruction: Connect the LDR/resistor junction to Arduino analog input A0.

steps.title: Power the divider
steps.instruction: Connect LDR VCC leg to Arduino 5V and the resistor's free leg to GND.

steps.title: Read light level
steps.instruction: Read the analog value at A0 and confirm it falls in the expected ambient-light range.

expected_measurements.description: Typical indoor ambient light ADC reading (0-1023 scale).

validation_rules.description: LDR and 10k resistor must both be present on the breadboard.
LDR OUT must connect to Arduino A0.
LDR VCC and divider resistor GND leg must be correctly powered.
ADC reading must fall within the expected ambient light range.

troubleshooting.reading_always_0: Check that LDR VCC is connected to 5V, not left floating.
troubleshooting.reading_always_1023: Check that the resistor's ground leg is actually connected to GND.
troubleshooting.no_change_with_light: Confirm the LDR itself (not a fixed resistor) is in the light-facing leg of the divider.
